Pan Man meets Super Hot

半即时制吸血鬼幸存者like，玩法很有趣但目前平衡性不太行。虽然游戏还在抢先体验未来可期，平衡性可以等更新，但看了看房东那个平衡性，说实话我不太抱期待。 1. 部分道具很需要其他道具的配合，例如跺脚等范围攻击没有香蕉皮的加范围很难打到人。然而由于道具池的随机规则，有时会遇到跺脚开局但一直随机不到香蕉皮，被垃圾被动填满格子导致拿不到香蕉皮的情况。建议学吸血鬼幸存者加个局外升级的重roll/ban道具功能，或者改进道具池机制，保证每次至少有1个选项是现有道具的升级而不是3个新道具。 2. 还是重roll问题，游戏内可以拿的重roll被动地位十分尴尬，8个栏位填满以后就基本没用了，等于少一个被动栏位。然而我拿一个垃圾被动也是亏一个被动格子，拿了重roll被动也是亏一个被动格子，那我要你干嘛呢？同上建议删掉改成局外升级。 3. 部分一次性被动道具看似画面十足实则难以发挥，例如复印机，作者明显是希望你在主力道具等级够高后拿复印机白嫖等级，然而由于上述道具池机制，你的主力等级高了以后被动槽往往已经填满了。 4. 本游戏没有幸存者和土豆兄弟那样局内掉落回血道具的机制，默认情况一局只有4次受伤机会，导致生存类道具几乎必定占一个格子。然而某些生存道具实在是幽默至极，例如加血上限的毛衣。角色自身没有回血机制，加25血上限就等于一次性的回25血。想要利用这25点血上限，只能再拿一个爱/葵花籽回血；然而单拿爱就足够保证生存，那小毛衣的意义是什么…… 5. 百合很强，爆米花很强，目前我拿过的道具里这两个远强于其他输出/生存道具，不排除我没拿过的道具里还有其他超模的。 6. Boss固定在10分钟刷新，但这个时间往往只够把一两个主力道具升到较高等级，其他道具往往只有一两级，纯来凑数的。Boss也很幽默，能被星星/黑洞这类机制道具直接秒杀几条命。 7. 角色只有初始道具不同，其他方面完全没区别，不像幸存者/土豆兄弟的角色会有属性/机制上的区别。 抛开这些平衡性问题，这个游戏玩法底子很好很有趣，和其他幸存者like一样大脑按摩，同时又不需要一直操作走位，可以随时切出去，很适合工作时候摸鱼玩。如果Steam有中评我会给中评，但看在抢先体验的份上先给个好评，虽然我不太期待作者的平衡性更新就是了。

Man... as a big fan of the developer (of [i]Luck Be a Landlord[/i] fame), I genuinely wish I could give [i]Maze Mice[/i] a full-hearted recommendation. Alas, where the game excels in production it falters in gameplay, specifically when comparing the experience with its roguelike peers. It's also worth noting that the developer has communicated an unlikelihood of improving the game beyond balancing and debugging. [b]Pros[/b] + Promising concept and loop, enough to consider [i]Maze Mice[/i] for a quick, casual gaming session every now and then. + Charming pixel art and a bopping (if limited) soundtrack. It’s clear an abundance of care went into illustrating the numerous mice, items, stages, and music. [b]Cons[/b] – All breadth, no depth. A lack of strategic variation and synergistic discovery restricts runs into feeling far too similar. The large roster of (exceedingly cute) mice play identically, while many of the items suffer from feeling dull or duplicative. – Linear unlockables, determined solely by playtime. Unlike others in the genre, [i]Maze Mice[/i] makes no effort to encourage the player to pivot to achieve anything. Every player unlocks everything in the same order, simply by accumulating score across runs. – Expensive, relative to its peers. All-time greats like [i]Halls of Torment[/i] and [i]Brotato[/i] are far richer in mechanics and replayability at a fraction of the cost.

cute! really clever fusion of genres, charming art, genuinely a super fun time killer of a game. why is this a negative review? well, because it needs a few things to actually shine here. On the design side, this is a "bullet heaven" type game -- a Vampire Survivor clone, in as many words -- mixed with a maze runner. works really surprisingly well as a genre mashup, and the weapons are designed to work well with it! but like VS, you have limited slots for upgrades when you level -- four weapons, and four support items. This one has NO rerolls by default... unless you take the "Recycle" support item, which drops rerolls as a powerup in the maze. This absolutely sucks. You cannot swap items when you select one in any way, so taking Recycles as a level-up option effectively screws you once you have your other 7 slots locked. HOWEVER, as your chosen mouse's main weapon may or may not benefit from damage, cooldown reduction, area of effect increase, etc.. you're ALSO heavily incentivized to pick an optimal build of support items and supplementary weapons, based on what you start with or have picked up so far. Since you can't reroll, you can easily get stuck with subweapons or items that are completely useless with your build, and as you have no way to avoid this besides first getting lucky enough to find Recycles and then permanently nerfing yourself by taking them, this encourages you to simply kill yourself the first time you're forced to pick a bad upgrade. This sucks! Just fix it; remove Recycles, as the support pool is already too bloated, and give limited rerolls per run. I understand if it seems too much like other games in the genre, but unfortunately, they all work like that for a reason. You can't avoid it. Sorry. The only other real complaint (and it is one) is that the music is great, but there are only... two? three? tracks that play in a run, and it can get a little monotonous that way. A couple more tracks would be really great to help make sessions feel less... drone-y. I must stress these are really my ONLY complaints; this is a killer little game! But the reroll issue is SO bad, and so encouraging of a degenerate strategy of constantly ending and restarting runs to get good picks, that it needs to be fixed for this to really have staying power. i have a few wins, and i'd love to go deeper into difficulty levels, but straight up, I don't want to play knowing that running on higher difficulty will only make it MORE necessary to suicide out of most of my attempts. Just fix that, and this is an incredible value proposition, and a charming game besides. (As an addendum, this gets an 11/10 from my cat. Jyn loves to sit and watch me play; i've never seen her so locked in on something boring like a screen, instead of something cool, like a bug running around outside. I think she's secretly cheering for the cats, but I understand.)

I actually have a Pacman rogue-like design doc created, from a few years back, so seeing this one pop up piqued my interest. Luckily, it's completely different from my own concept. Unfortunately, it's also confusing, doesn't ramp up properly, has limited replay value, and hits less hard than all of its inspirations. The best thing I can say about this one is that it's relaxing to play. You get into a sort of zen state as it's never especially challenging, but it is always moving and progressing. The ability to pause at any point is weird though. I don't like it, but I can see its appeal. Vampire Survivors doesn't include "endless" for a reason. The same reason why once you have a broken build in this game, it truly is endless (I discovered a broken build with Wheels within 3 hours of playing). Pacman Championship Edition adjusts the maze layout to keep things fresh whereas this game can have you going around in circles for minutes. And then you hit 10 minutes and it just sort of ends after a mindless boss battle. This needs a lot of content updates to be viable, but even so I don't think the initial gameplay loop is intriguing enough to return to. Despite what seems like a negative review, I'm still excited to what's next from this dev!

While not a bad game, I wouldn't recommend this as it gets stale very quickly. The game is missing multiple replayability roguelike elements from Vampire Survivor type games. It also doesn't feel nearly as polished or tuned. - No "final form" for upgrades/ no synergistic support + weapon combos so upgrading feels boring with no end goal. - Upgrades aren't tuned and are just simple value increases, this means certain upgrades like decreasing time of the shield are more powerful than others. - Only two enemy types - No post-game upgrade system

Other negative reviews have put it best, the idea is not bad but it gets stale real quick. The upgrades don't feel impactful and there's not any real synergies. If it were presented as just a 4-8 hour one off mini vampire survivors clone I could easily recommend it, but because of how the progression and achievements are structured, it's completely padded and designed to be a monotonous time sink. There are 30 characters all with their own 5 difficulty ascensions that need to be completed sequentially. The characters don't offer anything different in mechanics other than a starting upgrade which is trivial. The mice should just be skins and then let you pick a starting item. 30 characters, 5 tiers each, at 11ish minutes a run, this adds an unnecessary 28 hours bloat MINIMUM to an otherwise 8 hour game.

I really wanted to enjoy Maze Mice but it simply does not nail the gameplay like so many others in it's genre. Progression is purely based on how long you play, with no reward for focusing on specific builds or techniques. The types of enemies is very limited and doesn't ask you to change your gameplay. The maps do introduce a nice variance in how you play but it's not enough to carry the rest of the game. It's also unfortunate for Maze Mice that it's in a genre that seems to be hyper budget. I would recommend Halls of Torment or Vampire Survivors above this every day of the week, and they're both significantly cheaper.

First, let me get it out of the way: the gameplay is great, that’s not why I’m giving it a negative review, But I don’t want to sit here and rant about all of the things this game does wrong. I think the core idea is amazing… it’s just needs a little bit more polish. Starting with the positives. Music is amazing, as of right now I love it and hopefully I won’t get tired of it. The gameplay is also amazing. the usual survivors-like formula is plagued with the “kite enemies in circles” movement and this games pac-man structure adds an extra layer of depth (even if it is just running in circles but different). Now, onto the negatives: first, enemy variety. There are 2 enemies in the entire game (3 if you count the boss). One of them is super easy to dodge, the other phases through walls and will be the only one to hit you. I only played Enough to unlock 2/4 of the stages, and to my knowledge they have the same enemies. The last two stages might be different, but I doubt it. Next, the unlock system. You know how survivors-likes are known for their large amount of achievements and unlocks. This game has that too, but there’s one problem. Literally everything in the game is unlocked by points which carry over from run to run. You don’t get anything for beating the boss, you don’t get anything for playing endless, you don’t get anything for playing higher difficulties, and you don’t get anything for making unique builds. This ultimately makes progression feel flat. Why aren’t the stages locked behind beating the previous one. I had to beat the first stage 3 TIMES before I unlocked the second. Also, character roster. Of the characters I have unlocked. None of them have any sort of special ability or trait that makes them unique. The only mechanical difference between them is what upgrade they start with. If you replaced the character select screen with a menu that let you pick your starting item, it would 1, male characters obsolete, and 2, get rid of some of the annoying point unlocks. I don’t recommend you do this however. I like having multiple characters, it’s just that they don’t feel different from one another. 4th, difficulty levels. This game features an ascension style difficulty system with five levels of difficulty. However, the ascension levels don’t carry over from character to character, in order to unlock the hardest difficulty for a new character, you need to beat 4 30 minute+ runs. This whole system is made even worse by the fact that every character feels the exact same to play. Lastly, weapon feel. Almost Every single weapon in this game feels like it doesn’t deal any damage. They do deal damage, it’s just that the enemies are so tanky it requires a long time to kill one. This is probably to get the player to focus on the movement part of the game more, but it doesn’t feel good to get to the endgame, have lots of enemies on screen, and slowly kill a couple at a time. Additionally, if your weapon doesn’t hit the entire screen, you aren’t going to be killing the ghosts. Your movement is so restricted and their movement isn’t, so it’s much more difficult to line up a scenario where they get hit by something (especially when you are getting chased by a horde) Ultimately, I think this could be a great game, but it needs a lot of work done to it. I really didn’t want this to be a negative review, but I just can’t. After the first couple of runs, I’m just not having fun.

Maze Mice is a survivors-like game meshed together with Pac-man. You move about a maze collecting XP orbs being chased by cats, and as you level up you improve your skills just like in any other survivors-like to kill the boss. Enemies only move when you do, so you don't need to stress about making quick decisions. Your mouse can have up to 4 weapon skills, and 4 support skills, and they can all be leveled up a various amount of times. At the end of 10 minutes of gameplay, a big spooky ghost cat boss appears, and upon killing it you win the run (and can choose to play endless if so desired). The core gameplay concept is sound. Its a pretty engaging gameplay loop. And yet, I am not reccomending this game. The big problem with the game is that it has next to no depth. There are a grand total of two enemy types (and 1 boss) throughout the entire game. There are 4 maps, all which largely play the same. There are many skills, most of which all play the same. Like, there's one support upgrade which increases the amount of XP you get. A second support upgrade that makes XP orbs dropped provide more XP. A third upgrade that makes more XP orbs spawn on the ground. They're all just flavors of the same thing, and largely don't matter which one you pick. There are many, many, many characters, and every single one of them is identical except for starting with a different skill at level 1. It just adds to the bloat of the game and doesn't add any depth. Does it matter if you start with Knitting Needles at level 1 instead of Hairball? Not really. You can make builds mostly the same every single time, and they all play out the same way. Coming from the Luck be a Landlord developers, I expected a game with a lot more depth. But right now all the game has is a shallow layer on top. That shallow layer is solid - the core gameplay is fun. But without more depth there isn't any staying power to keep wanting to play the game,

Yeah this game is sort of half baked. The idea is cool with the whole nothing moves if you don't move, but everything else is about as bare bones as they come. The different levels are terrible and you'll find yourself going back to the first one a lot. The different mice are all the same with just a different starting skill, but nothing else. There are 3 total characters in the game who have slightly different colors to indicate they are tanky or not and there's only 1 boss character that I've seen thus far. That's all bad, but the worst is the lack of banishes or skips in the game too as the item pool is just saturated with items that are just really bad and you can only equip 4 weapons and 4 artifacts in a run. I got this as I liked the idea and really enjoy luck be a landlord, but they stepped into something I don't think they really understand and it didn't make for a very good game. I wouldn't recommend this for anything over $2-3 unless there is a major patch rework in the future.

Cool idea but ultimately not very interesting to play, it gets boring relatively quickly. Progression feels aimless because you don't actually know how or when you unlock new things (or at least I can't figure it out). Unlockable characters don't really introduce anything new since the only difference is the starting weapon. The UI is unpleasant to use. The buttons don't stand out well, they're not highlighted well when selected and they're extremely spread out on opposite ends of the screen which maximises mouse travel distance for no reason. Some of them are also small (e.g. difficulty selection). This combination makes the menus, which should be simple, feel overly cumbersome. I love that this game tries something new and if it was cheaper I would probably be more charitable, but selling this for 10€ at full price is outright criminal.

I totally missed the [b]Vampire Survivors[/b] hype and addiction, so this is my version of that. I'd definitely say it's much more like that than the arcade-y [b]Pac-Man[/b] experience the screenshots make it out to be. You kill cats and collect pellets to earn experience and level up. Every level, you draw three abilities and pick one to upgrade. You have one life, so when you die, the run resets completely. Having a good run is heavily dependent on synergizing abilities, but also a bit of luck in drawing good options. If you've played any post-[b]Vampire Survivors[/b] roguelike, all of this will probably sound very familiar. The bullet-time mechanic - [i]everything only moves when you move[/i] - was a great addition and makes the game feel strategic. You can pause at any moment to weigh your options. Do you lure an enemy closer? Do you make a dash for a pellet or pickup? Do you intentionally take a hit to reach a goal? You have time to think through all of those decisions. But once they become second nature, the game still flows naturally and never feels interrupted. There are a lot of [i]characters[/i], and you unlock them faster than you'll actually complete runs with them. But they don't really do much beyond giving you a fixed starting ability. The only one that significantly changed how I played was Humphrey. Otherwise, they mostly serve as fun excuses to keep playing with slight variations and work toward more achievements. There are also four maps, and I eventually completed runs on all of them. But honestly, I liked the first map, Attic, the most and spent most of my time there. Definitely a [i]play a little at a time[/i] kind of game. Simple enough to jump in and out of quickly. Addicting enough to keep saying "one more run". But also: beware of burnout.

I'm a bit on the fence for this game. The mechanics are a bit thin as there are 2 enemy types and most levels involve you running around in a circle to herd and keep distance from the ghost enemies while the ones trailing you mostly keep you from going backward. Selecting some healing items and leveling them up is the only rule you need to stay alive, otherwise basically any weapon will help keep the enemies down to ensure your movement options remain open, though the ghosts are usually more difficult to deal with. There are only a few levels, too many characters for some reason that dont differ significantly, and I am still unlocking weapons/support gear which have interesting quirks. Would have liked to see the game require a bit more thought and execution to play, maybe with more enemy behaviors or hazards, but I admit I'm not sure if the design would support it easily. Maybe challenges to complete a run with certain pre-set builds or modifiers. Ultimately, I guess I like it enough as I enjoy the music and playing with new weapons/items. After I unlock everything, I cannot imagine having much reason to play further.

As close to an unfinished game as it gets without being actually unfinished. 4 levels, 2 enemy types, 1 boss that is just a larger one of the enemy types. That's it. A bunch of unlockable items, many of which aren't especially useful. Unlockable characters that only differ by starting item, so they are all interchangeable. In their 1.0 release notes the developer notes that the game didn't sell well, which more or less backs up the pseudo unfinished state of the game. It's a shame, the game has solid bones but needs more meat.
